chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him): Who are the Family of Muhammad? He said: His descendants. I said: Who are his Ahl al-Bayt? He said: The Imams, the appointed successors. I said: Who is his Itra? He said: The People of the Cloak. I said: Who is his Umma? He said: The believers who affirmed what he brought from God, Mighty and Majestic, those who hold fast to the Two Weighty Things which they were commanded to hold fast to: the Book of God and his progeny, his Ahl al-Bayt, from whom God has removed uncleanliness and purified with a thorough purification. And these two are the vicegerents over the nation after the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).

key_terms.آل: Aal - Family/Clan of the Prophet, defined here as his descendants (dhurriyya)
key_terms.أمة: Umma - Nation, defined here as the believers who hold fast to the Two Weighty Things
key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahl al-Bayt - People of the House, defined here as the Imams and appointed successors (awsiya)
key_terms.الثقلين: Thaqalayn - The Two Weighty Things: the Book of God and the Prophetic household
key_terms.عترة: Itra - Progeny, defined here specifically as the People of the Cloak (Ashab al-Aba)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Aal Muhammad, Ahl al-Bayt, Itra, and Umma according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Abu Basir asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to precisely define four key terms related to the Prophet Muhammad. The Imam distinguishes between Aal Muhammad (his descendants), Ahl al-Bayt (the appointed Imams/successors), Itra (the People of the Cloak, i.e. Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn), and his Umma (the believers who hold fast to both the Quran and the Prophetic household). This was a crucial clarification for the early Shia community, as these terms carried significant legal and theological weight in determining religious authority after the Prophet.
